note: generation.* is real mlx_lm.generate() decode throughput/memory on plain fp16 caches (no VeloxQuant cache wiring — none of the pool code sits in this decode's hot path). allocator_replay.* re-plays the block pool and naive baseline at this model's *real* (n_layers, n_kv_heads, head_dim, generation_length), so the allocation-count/reuse/fragmentation numbers reflect a real model's real decode length rather than an arbitrary synthetic one. tokens_per_sec under allocator_replay is allocator-side append throughput on synthetic zero-filled vectors, not generation.generation_tps; mx.zeros() is lazy/cheap in MLX so the naive baseline's raw allocator throughput here is not penalized for the malloc/free churn a real allocator would pay under memory pressure or an eager backend — read allocations_per_request and n_reused as the honest signal, the same caveat as benchmark_block_pool.py.
